# BAD-044 — Split web/app.js (1909 lines) into app-<part>.js classic scripts

## Brief
Plan: [[docs/spikes/bad-036/web-app|web-app spike]] (Roseval, BADS-036).

Proposed: twelve contiguous classic scripts at the top level of web/ named app-<part>.js (shell, util, library, catalog, casting, takes, files, session, tableread, stage, settings), tagged before booth.js, with web/app.js kept as the entry (boot, Android Back, window.bootApp) and the last tag of its group. Two files over 250 are argued (app-library 344, app-stage 276). Dry run: 1909 of 1909 lines covered once, every piece parses, a vm load in tag order raises nothing, and a paragraph-level move check passes and fails on a one-token rewrite. Files stay at web/ top level because test/web-ids.test.js reads web/ non-recursively; scripts/build-web.js already copies and stamps new files.

Cross-ticket: test/web-guest-mode.test.js must read a file list derived from web/index.html's script tags. The web/app.js, web/booth.js and web/collabweb.js splits all need that helper; whichever lands first adds it and the others reuse it. The duplicate top-level name sweep covers all three families.

Verification: the move check, npm test, npm run web and npm run web:build, a 375px phone-layout pass, and npm run web:local for the collab paths.

**Gate.** Queued until Eric approves the proposed file layout in the spike. Phase 2 does not start before that approval, and an approval that changes the layout is written into the spike's section 4 first.

**Rules for Phase 2, from BAD-036.** Split by responsibility; 250 lines is where a file gets a second look, not a cap, and every file left over 250 is argued in the spike's section 6. Every PR is a pure move: no statement is edited, a bug found on the way is its own ticket, and the spike's behaviour-preservation check (section 8) runs on every PR. The public surface in section 2 is the compatibility contract and does not change. Extraction order follows section 9: shared constants, types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components or handlers, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator. Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier for the files touched, quoted in each PR.

## Size, persona and model decision
Eric's call, 2026-09-15: the spike's layout is approved as proposed (section 4 unchanged: eleven app-<part>.js files plus app.js as the last tag of its group, app-library and app-stage kept whole), and Phase 2 lands as ONE pull request for the whole split instead of section 9's eight, with the section 8 recipe as its proof. One engineer on opus in a worktree on feat/bad-044-split-web-app after bash scripts/worktree-init.sh, then a reviewer on opus (Fable's weekly limit is reached, Eric 2026-09-15) who reruns the move check and the load-order probes before it lands. No member, child or probe runs on fable.
